PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-what-actually-how-2|COREMERCH guide to payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Fonts online

Stripe offers payment processing in 46 countries, but it's not available everywhere, and when it is, you still have to comply with its terms; PayPal claims to operate in 200 markets, but its account suspension can hold funds for up to 180 days; Gumroad is a full-service platform for creators, but it's not a base-layer infrastructure solution, and Lemon Squeezy is a simplified alternative to Stripe, but it still has restrictions on country availability.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Stripe operates in 46 countries, but it excludes many others, including Nigeria, Ghana, and Pakistan; PayPal is available in more countries than Stripe, but its account suspension can still freeze funds for up to 180 days; Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy have restrictions on country availability, and neither is a viable option for creators in restricted countries; in contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure like Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is a base-layer solution that gives creators full control over their digital commerce stacks, regardless of country restrictions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Stripe's payment processing fees range from 2.9% + 30 cents per transaction to 1% + 5 cents for high-volume sellers; PayPal's fees range from 2.9% + 30 cents to 3.5% + 15 cents for domestic transactions; Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy have lower fees, but they're still not a viable option for high-volume sellers; sovereign commerce infrastructure like Edge Commerce Stack ($197) charges 0.5% fees for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, and it's a flat rate, with no surprise fees or restrictive terms.
Stripe excludes many countries, including Nigeria, Ghana, and Pakistan.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With Stripe, you're at the mercy of its terms, and you have to comply with its payment processing requirements; with PayPal, you're at risk of account suspension and frozen funds; with Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy, you're limited to their platform features and restrictions; in contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure like Edge Commerce Stack ($197) gives creators full ownership and control over their digital commerce stacks, with automatic crypto payment verification and instant product delivery, and it's a base-layer solution that's not dependent on any third-party platform.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you're a high-volume seller who needs fast payment processing and low fees, sovereign commerce infrastructure like Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is the best choice; if you're a creator who needs full control over their digital commerce stacks and can handle the technical setup, Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is the way to go; if you're in a restricted country, Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is the only viable option that gives you full infrastructure sovereignty.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

The direct answer is NOWPayments combined with a sovereign commerce stack. NOWPayments is a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 coins, charges 0.5% per transaction, and sends a webhook to your backend the moment payment confirms on-chain. Your backend — a Cloudflare Worker in Stack 02, a Google Apps Script Web App in Stack 01 — receives the webhook, verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email automatically. There is no platform that can suspend your access, no compliance team that can flag your account, no payout schedule that delays your revenue, and no company that can change the rules on you tomorrow.
PayPal's account suspension can freeze funds for up to 180 days.

If you're looking for a way to sell digital products without relying on restricted platforms like Stripe, Gumroad, or Lemon Squeezy, or if you're in a country where PayPal is not available, Edge Commerce Stack ($197) is the base-layer infrastructure solution that's right for you; check out our products at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Accept that no workaround inside conventional payment infrastructure is durable — platforms actively close gaps as they discover them. Create a NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as your starting point — these cover the widest range of buyers in restricted markets. Choose your stack: Stack 01 for a self-deployed free setup using GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script, Stack 02 for the Edge Stack deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours. Configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint URL in your IPN settings pointing to your backend. Upload your product files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Complete a real mainnet test transaction and confirm the full pipeline: webhook received, transaction verified on-chain, order logged, delivery email sent, download link working. Share your store URL only after the mainnet test passes cleanly.
